bites.title: Make your grays
bites.body: Painters mix grays on the palette. Here's the digital version: paint black and white side by side, smear them together, then pick the gray you need out of the smear.

bites.title: Black and white
bites.body: In the empty space at the bottom, paint a black blob. Press {key:toggle_fg_bg|X} and paint a white blob touching it. (Paint on the gray margin if white disappears on white.)

bites.title: Grab a blender
bites.body: Switch to a blending brush. Pick one from Brush Presets, or let me grab one.

bites.title: Make mud
bites.body: Drag back and forth across the border until you get a long smooth gradient. Somewhere in that mud is every gray you'll need.

bites.title: Pick about a third
bites.body: Hold Ctrl and click in the smear (or use {key:KritaSelected/KisToolColorSampler|P}) to grab a gray around 33%.

bites.title: Paint box 4
bites.body: Switch back to a normal brush ({key:KritaShape/KisToolBrush|B}, Basic-1) and fill box 4 (33%) with your picked gray.

bites.title: The whole ladder, from mud
bites.body: Every box, every gray picked out of your mud. Squint at the top row versus yours.

bites.title: 11 cleared
bites.body: Mix, smear, pick, paint. That's how oil painters think, and it works just as well here.
